content.text:
### Configure Web App Manifest with vite-plugin-pwa

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/docs/blob/main/guide/pwa-minimal-requirements.md

Minimal VitePWA plugin configuration that adds a Web App Manifest with required entries: name, short_name, description, theme_color, and 192x192 and 512x512 icons. The scope is omitted and defaults to the Vite base option (default '/'). You must provide all the icons and images referenced.

```ts
import { VitePWA } from 'vite-plugin-pwa'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    VitePWA({
      includeAssets: ['favicon.ico', 'apple-touch-icon.png', 'mask-icon.svg'],
      manifest: {
        name: 'My Awesome App',
        short_name: 'MyApp',
        description: 'My Awesome App description',
        theme_color: '#ffffff',
        icons: [
          {
            src: 'pwa-192x192.png',
            sizes: '192x192',
            type: 'image/png'
          },
          {
            src: 'pwa-512x512.png',
            sizes: '512x512',
            type: 'image/png'
          }
        ]
      }
    })
  ]
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure vite-plugin-pwa with registerType autoUpdate

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/docs/blob/main/guide/index.md

Minimal configuration for vite-plugin-pwa in your vite.config.js or vite.config.ts file. This enables generation of the Web App Manifest, service worker, and registration script.

```ts
import { VitePWA } from 'vite-plugin-pwa'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    VitePWA({ registerType: 'autoUpdate' })
  ]
})
```

--------------------------------

### PWA manifest minimal requirements (icons and scope)

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/docs/blob/main/guide/pwa-minimal-requirements.md

Lists the Web App Manifest entries required for installability: the plugin derives `scope` from the Vite `base` option (default `/`), and `192x192` plus `512x512` icons are mandatory — this clarifies the manifest icon and scope/start_url behavior for installable PWAs.

```markdown
Your application [Web App Manifest](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Manifest) **must** have the following entries:
- a scope: omitted here for simplicity, the `vite-plugin-pwa` plugin will use the `Vite` base option to configure it (default is `/`)
- a name
- a short description
- a description
- a `theme_color`: **must match** the configured one on `Entry Point theme-color`
- an icon with `192x192` size
- an icon with `512x512` size
```

--------------------------------

### Advanced (injectManifest) > Custom Service worker > Plugin Configuration

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/docs/blob/main/guide/inject-manifest.md

You **must** configure `strategies: 'injectManifest'` in `vite-plugin-pwa` plugin options in your `vite.config.ts` file:

--------------------------------

### Vite PWA > Configuring vite-plugin-pwa

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/docs/blob/main/guide/index.md

If you want to check it in `dev`, add the `devOptions` option to the plugin configuration (you will have the [Web App Manifest][webmanifest] and the generated service worker):
```ts
import { VitePWA } from 'vite-plugin-pwa'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    VitePWA({
      registerType: 'autoUpdate',
      devOptions: {
        enabled: true
      }
    })
  ]
})
```

## Objective
- Erstelle eine moderne, schicke Todo-App als PWA mit Vite.js gemäß den Anforderungen in todo_prompt.md

## Requirements
- Vite als Build-Tool
- PWA (Progressive Web App) installierbar
- Modernes, schlichtes UI, responsive für Desktop und Mobile
- Light Mode und Dark Mode mit vollständigem Theme-Wechsel
- Sichtbarer Toggle zwischen Light und Dark Mode
- Theme nach Neuladen erhalten
- Todo-Funktionen: hinzufügen, erledigen/unerledigen, löschen, bearbeiten
- Filter: Alle, Offen, Erledigt
- Anzeige der Anzahl offener Todos
- Todos nach Neuladen erhalten (localStorage)
- Keine externe Datenbank oder Backend
- Alle Buttons und Eingaben müssen funktionieren
- Keine nur optisch vorhandenen Funktionen

## Decisions
- React TypeScript Template für Vite-Projekt verwendet
- vite-plugin-pwa für PWA-Funktionalität konfiguriert
- localStorage für Persistenz von Todos und Theme verwendet
- Eigene TodoApp.tsx-Komponente erstellt

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite-Projekt mit React TypeScript scaffolded in todo-app Verzeichnis
- npm install und vite-plugin-pwa installiert
- vite.config.ts um VitePWA-Plugin erweitert mit Manifest-Konfiguration
- TodoApp.tsx mit allen Todo-Funktionen (add, toggle, delete, edit, filter, count, dark mode) erstellt
- App.tsx vereinfacht um TodoApp-Komponente

### Active
- CSS-Styling für Todo-App noch nicht implementiert (App.css und index.css müssen angepasst werden)

### Blocked
- Keine

## Next Move
1. CSS-Styling für die Todo-App in App.css und index.css implementieren (modernes Design, abgerundete Karten, Dark Mode)
2. App lokal starten und alle Funktionen testen
3. Production Build erstellen und verifizieren
4. PWA-Installation und Offline-Funktionalität prüfen

- /Users/cedi/Clouds/Projekte/KI/LLM-Bench/tests/todo-app/Kolibri-1 (IQ4_XS)/todo-app/package.json: Abhängigkeiten

# Skill: built-in-browser

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working. Claude does not tell the person that they missed it or could not see it, because Claude cannot tell what they were watching.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, Claude usually cannot tell whether the person is reading this conversation in the desktop app, on the claude.ai website or on a phone, and the shortcut and the globe icon work only in the desktop app, so before those steps Claude says that if they are not in the Claude desktop app on the computer whose browser Claude is using, they need to open this conversation there first. Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

## Objective
- Erstelle eine moderne, schicke Todo-App als PWA mit Vite.js gemäß den Anforderungen in todo_prompt.md

## Requirements
- Vite als Build-Tool
- PWA installierbar
- Modernes, schlichtes UI, responsive für Desktop und Mobile
- Light Mode und Dark Mode mit vollständigem Theme-Wechsel
- Sichtbarer Toggle zwischen Light und Dark Mode
- Theme nach Neuladen erhalten
- Todo-Funktionen: hinzufügen, erledigen/unerledigen, löschen, bearbeiten
- Filter: Alle, Offen, Erledigt
- Anzeige der Anzahl offener Todos
- Todos nach Neuladen erhalten (localStorage)
- Keine externe Datenbank oder Backend
- Alle Buttons und Eingaben müssen funktionieren
- Keine nur optisch vorhandenen Funktionen
- Verwende Jev-Skill bei Bedarf für Library-/API-Verifikation
- Verwende frontend-design-Skill für UI-Gestaltung

## Decisions
- React TypeScript Template für Vite-Projekt verwendet
- vite-plugin-pwa für PWA-Funktionalität konfiguriert
- localStorage für Persistenz von Todos und Theme verwendet
- Eigene TodoApp.tsx-Komponente erstellt
- Fehlende Dev-Dependencies (@types/react, @vitejs/plugin-react, @types/react-dom) installiert

## Objective
- Create a modern, sleek Todo app as a PWA with Vite.js per todo_prompt.md requirements.

## Requirements
- Vite as build tool
- PWA installable
- Modern, simple UI, responsive for desktop and mobile
- Light Mode and Dark Mode with full theme switch
- Visible toggle between Light and Dark Mode
- Theme persists after reload
- Todo functions: add, toggle, delete, edit
- Filter: All, Offen, Erledigt
- Display count of open todos
- Todos persist after reload via localStorage
- No external database or backend
- All buttons and inputs must function
- No purely cosmetic functions
- Use Jev-Skill for Library-/API-Verifikation if needed
- Use frontend-design-Skill for UI-Gestaltung

## Decisions

- vite-plugin-pwa for PWA functionality configured
- localStorage for persistence of todos and theme used

- darkMode useState initialized from localStorage

- Vite as build tool

- Light Mode and Dark Mode with full theme switch

- Todo functions: add, toggle, delete, edit

- Display count of open todos
- Todos persist after reload via localStorage
- No external database or backend

- Use frontend-design-Skill for UI-Gestaltung

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/vite-plugin-pwa/blob/main/src/types.ts

Defines the schema for each entry of the `manifest.icons` array: `src` (the icon file, e.g. an .svg), `type` (a free-form string media type such as `image/svg+xml`), `sizes` (a free-form string such as `192x192` or `any`), and `purpose` (e.g. `any`, `maskable`).

/**

 */
export interface IconResource {
  sizes?: string
  src: string
  type?: string
  /**

  purpose?: StringLiteralUnion<IconPurpose> | IconPurpose[]
}

Since `vite-plugin-pwa` plugin uses [workbox-build](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/modules/workbox-build/) node library to build the service worker, it will only include `css`, `js` and `html` resources in the manifest precache (check the `globPatterns` entry in [GlobPartial](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/reference/workbox-build/#type-GlobPartial)).

`workbox-build` node library is file based, that is, it will traverse the build output folder of your application. `Vite` will generate your build in the `dist` folder, and so, `workbox-build` will traverse the `dist` folder adding all resources found in it to the service worker's precache manifest.

## Objective
- Create a modern, sleek Todo app as a PWA with Vite.js

## Requirements
- Vite as build tool
- PWA installable
- Modern, simple UI, responsive for desktop and mobile
- Light Mode and Dark Mode with full theme switch
- Theme persists after reload
- Todo functions: add, toggle, delete, edit
- Filter: All, Offen, Erledigt
- Display count of open todos
- Todos persist after reload via localStorage
- No external database or backend
- All buttons and inputs must function
- No purely cosmetic functions
- Use Jev-Skill for Library-/API-Verifikation if needed
- Use frontend-design-Skill for UI-Gestaltung

- React TypeScript Template for Vite project used

## Objective
- Create a modern, sleek Todo app as a PWA with Vite.js

## Requirements
- Vite as build tool
- PWA installable
- Modern, simple UI, responsive for desktop and mobile
- Light Mode and Dark Mode with full theme switch
- Theme persists after reload
- Todo functions: add, toggle, delete, edit
- Filter: All, Open, Done
- Display count of open todos
- Todos persist after reload via localStorage
- No external database or backend
- All buttons and inputs must function
- No purely cosmetic functions
- Use Jev-Skill for Library-/API-Verifikation if needed
- Use frontend-design-Skill for UI-Gestaltung

## Decisions
- React TypeScript Template for Vite project used
- vite-plugin-pwa for PWA functionality configured
- localStorage for persistence of todos and theme used
- Custom TodoApp.tsx component created
- Missing Dev-Dependencies (@types/react, @types/react-dom, @vitejs/plugin-react) installed
- darkMode useState initialized from localStorage
- Todo initialization moved from useEffect to useState initializer for correct first render
- PWA icons changed from missing PNG to existing SVG (icons.svg) with purpose "any maskable"
- Added `:root.dark` CSS block in index.css to handle dark mode via class toggle
- Dark mode media query updated to use `:root:not(.dark)` to avoid overriding user theme preference

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite project with React TypeScript scaffolded
- npm install and vite-plugin-pwa installed
- vite.config.ts extended with VitePWA plugin (SVG icons)
- TodoApp.tsx with all Todo-Funktionen created (add, toggle, delete, edit)
- App.tsx simplified
- TypeScript-Fehler resolved
- Production Build successful
- CSS-Styling implemented
- Basic UI interaction test: typed "Test todo" and clicked Add; todo appeared

- Todo persistence after reload via localStorage verified (manual set and "Persistence Test 2")
- Added todo "Test Save" and confirmed visible in list

- Relevant files read; skills attempted to load

## Objective
- Create a modern, sleek Todo app as a PWA with Vite.js

## Requirements
- Vite as build tool
- PWA installable
- Modern, simple UI, responsive for desktop and mobile
- Light Mode and Dark Mode with full theme switch
- Theme persists after reload
- Todo functions: add, toggle, delete, edit
- Filter: All, Open, Done
- Display count of open todos
- Todos persist after reload via localStorage
- No external database or backend
- All buttons and inputs must function
- No purely cosmetic functions
- Use Jev-Skill for Library-/API-Verifikation if needed
- Use frontend-design-Skill for UI-Gestaltung

## Decisions
- React TypeScript Template for Vite project used
- vite-plugin-pwa for PWA functionality configured
- localStorage for persistence of todos and theme used
- Custom TodoApp.tsx component created
- Missing Dev-Dependencies (@types/react, @types/react-dom, @vitejs/plugin-react) installed
- darkMode useState initialized from localStorage
- Todo initialization moved from useEffect to useState initializer for correct first render
- PWA icons changed from missing PNG to existing SVG (icons.svg) with purpose "any maskable"
- Added `:root.dark` CSS block in index.css to handle dark mode via class toggle
- Dark mode media query updated to use `:root:not(.dark)` to avoid overriding user theme preference

## Work State

- Vite project with React TypeScript scaffolded
- npm install and vite-plugin-pwa installed
- vite.config.ts extended with VitePWA plugin (SVG icons)

- App.tsx simplified
- TypeScript-Fehler resolved
- Production Build successful
- CSS-Styling implemented
- Basic UI interaction test: typed "Test todo" and clicked Add; todo appeared
- Playwright tests: dark mode toggle clicked, todos added and deleted, filter buttons clicked
- Delete function verified for "Test Delete" todo
- Dark mode theme persistence after reload verified
- Todo persistence after reload via localStorage verified (manual set and "Persistence Test 2")
- Added todo "Test Save" and confirmed visible in list
- Edit function verified using Playwright (prompt dialog handled with "Updated Text")
- Dev server restarted after vite.config.ts change
- Relevant files read; skills attempted to load
- Dark mode CSS fix applied in index.css

### Active

### Manifest icon resource type (IconResource)

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/vite-plugin-pwa/blob/main/src/types.ts

Defines the schema for each entry of the `manifest.icons` array: `src` (the icon file, e.g. an .svg), `type` (a free-form string media type such as `image/svg+xml`), `sizes` (a free-form string such as `192x192` or `any`), and `purpose` (e.g. `any`, `maskable`).

```typescript
/**
 * @see https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#manifest-image-resources
 */
export interface IconResource {
  sizes?: string
  src: string
  type?: string
  /**
   * **NOTE**: string values for backward compatibility with the old type.
   */
  purpose?: StringLiteralUnion<IconPurpose> | IconPurpose[]
}
```

--------------------------------

### Add maskable icon to Web App Manifest

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/vite-plugin-pwa/blob/main/docs/guide/pwa-minimal-requirements.md

Optional manifest icons entry that adds a third icon with purpose 'any maskable' to the required 192x192 and 512x512 icons. This is not required to meet PWA minimal requirements.

```ts
icons: [
  {
    src: 'pwa-192x192.png',
    sizes: '192x192',
    type: 'image/png'
  },
  {
    src: 'pwa-512x512.png',
    sizes: '512x512',
    type: 'image/png'
  },
  {
    src: 'pwa-512x512.png',
    sizes: '512x512',
    type: 'image/png',
    purpose: 'any maskable'
  }
]
```

--------------------------------

### PWA Minimal Requirements > Icons / Images

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/vite-plugin-pwa/blob/main/docs/guide/pwa-minimal-requirements.md

For `manifest` icons entry, you will need to create `pwa-192x192.png`, and `pwa-512x512.png` icons. The icons specified above are the minimum required to meet PWA, that is, icons with `192x192` and `512x512` resolutions (last one duplicated for `purpose: 'any maskable'` if you want to add it, it is not required).

We suggest you to create a svg or png icon (if it is a png icon, with the maximum resolution possible) for your application and use it to generate a favicon package in [Favicon Generator](https://realfavicongenerator.net/).

For `mask-icon` in the entry point, use the svg or the png used to generate the favicon package.

Once generated, download the ZIP and use `android-*` icons for `pwa-*`:
- use `android-chrome-192x192.png` for `pwa-192x192.png`
- use `android-chrome-512x512.png` for `pwa-512x512.png`
- `apple-touch-icon.png` is `apple-touch-icon.png`
- `favicon.ico` is `favicon.ico`

Source: https://github.com/vite-pwa/vite-plugin-pwa/blob/main/src/pwa-assets/config.ts

The loadAssetsGeneratorContext function reads the SVG image file and passes it together with the preset (e.g., 'minimal-2023') to the @vite-pwa/assets-generator instructions() API, which generates all icon definitions (favicon, transparent, maskable, apple, appleSplashScreen) from the source SVG.

const imageName = relative(publicDir, imageFile)
const imageOutDir = dirname(resolve(outDir, imageName))

const xhtml = userHeadLinkOptions?.xhtml === true
const includeId = userHeadLinkOptions?.includeId === true
const assetsInstructions = await instructions({
  imageResolver: () => readFile(imageFile),
  imageName,
  preset,
